title: B2+ · L47 — Wellness & mental health vocabulary
description: Vocabulario de wellness y salud mental: burnout, boundaries, mindfulness, self-care, therapy language.

questions.prompt: Colega dice: 'I'm completely exhausted — I can't even open my laptop.'
questions.question: She's describing:
questions.explanation: Burnout = agotamiento cronico fisico + emocional + cognitivo por trabajo prolongado sin recuperacion. Recognized por la OMS como occupational phenomenon. Diferente de 'tired' (temporal) o 'stressed' (agudo). Palabra clave en HR y wellbeing.
examples: Classic burnout signs: cynicism, exhaustion, and reduced efficacy.
I hit full burnout after eighteen months of that pace. → testimonio personal

questions.prompt: Tu terapeuta te dice: 'You need to set clearer ___ with your manager.'
questions.question: Complete:
questions.explanation: 'Boundaries' es el termino estandar en therapy/wellness discourse. 'Limits' es correcto pero mas restrictivo/negativo. 'Walls' implica cerrarse totalmente (unhealthy). 'Borders' es geografico. 'Setting boundaries' es una colocacion casi obligatoria.
examples: I've set a hard boundary: no work Slack after 7pm.
Setting boundaries isn't rude — it's self-preservation. → therapy talk moderno

questions.statement: 'Mindfulness' means constantly thinking about your problems.
questions.explanation: FALSO. Mindfulness = atencion consciente al momento presente SIN juicio. Es lo OPUESTO a rumiar problemas. Practica derivada de traditions budistas, popularizada por Jon Kabat-Zinn. Confusion tipica es equipararla con 'thinking a lot'.
examples: Mindfulness is noticing without reacting — just observing the breath.
Even five minutes of mindfulness before bed changes my sleep. → habit real

questions.prompt: Amiga cuenta que ha empezado terapia.
questions.question: 'Self-care' means:
options: Deliberate practices to maintain your wellbeing.
questions.explanation: Self-care = practicas deliberadas para mantener bienestar (sleep, exercise, boundaries, therapy, hobbies). No es 'selfish' y no se reduce a skincare/spa (uso comercializado). Termino usado en mental health profesional y en cultura popular.
examples: Real self-care is boring: sleep, water, walks, saying no.
Self-care isn't a bubble bath — it's a therapy appointment. → reframe honesto

questions.text: I've been feeling completely drained lately, so I finally booked a session with a therapist to work through it.
questions.explanation: Discurso muy autentico de wellness discourse. 'Feeling drained' (colocacion tipica), 'work through it' (phrasal verb clave en therapy). Nota en hablado: 'I've been' se contrae fuerte ('ivbin'), y 'work through it' funde 'through it' en 'throo-git'.
examples: I've been drained for weeks — I booked therapy this morning.
Talking through it with a professional made all the difference.

questions.prompt: Manager en 1:1 pregunta como estas realmente.
questions.question: 'I'm overwhelmed' means:
options: There's too much to handle and I can't cope.
questions.explanation: 'Overwhelmed' = sobrepasado por cantidad/intensidad. Emocion valida y precisa; mas socialmente aceptable que 'estoy en crisis'. Se usa en trabajo, parenting, life admin. Colocaciones: 'feel overwhelmed by', 'get overwhelmed'.
examples: Honestly, I'm feeling overwhelmed by the workload this quarter.
I get overwhelmed when there are too many decisions at once. → auto-conocimiento

questions.prompt: Empareja cada termino de wellness/mental health con su definicion:
questions.explanation: Vocabulario nucleo de wellness discourse anglosajon. 'Grounding' es tecnica especifica (5-4-3-2-1 senses) para pausar spirals de ansiedad. Todos son terminos que ya salen naturalmente en conversacion cotidiana, no solo en clinica.
examples: When I feel a panic spike, I use the grounding technique — five things I can see.
Anxiety and stress aren't the same thing clinically. → precision therapeutica

questions.target: Honestly, I hit a wall last month — pure burnout. I've since started therapy, cut my hours, and I'm slowly getting back to myself.
questions.explanation: Discurso wellness personal muy actual. 'Hit a wall' (idiom para colapso), 'pure burnout' (intensifier), 'getting back to myself' (recovery language). Estructura: reconocer el problema + acciones tomadas + progreso. Muy comun en podcasts y therapy accounts.
examples: I hit a wall in March, and I've been rebuilding ever since.
Therapy plus fewer hours got me back to myself. → arc de recovery

questions.prompt: Podcast de wellness usa el termino 'triggered'.
questions.question: Being 'triggered' by something means:
options: Having an intense emotional reaction, often from past pain.
questions.explanation: 'Triggered' (uso psicologico) = reaccion emocional intensa activada por estimulo asociado a trauma pasado. Termino tecnico usado ahora en habla cotidiana. Precaucion: uso casual ('everything triggers me') puede banalizar el uso clinico serio.
examples: That song still triggers me — it takes me back to that year.
Certain tones of voice trigger her from her old boss. → trauma cotidiano

questions.statement: 'Cope' and 'deal with' are close synonyms in wellness contexts.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Cope with' y 'deal with' se usan intercambiablemente para 'manejar algo dificil'. Sutileza: 'cope' implica mas la carga emocional, 'deal with' es mas neutral. 'I can't cope' = emocionalmente saturada; 'I can't deal' = version informal muy comun.
examples: I honestly can't cope with another meeting today.
She's dealing with a lot right now, cut her some slack. → tono empatico

questions.prompt: Sesion de terapia: 'Let's ___ what came up for you this week.'
questions.question: Complete:
questions.explanation: 'Explore' es el verbo caracteristico del therapy discourse. Sugiere curiosidad, no juicio ni prisa por resolver. 'Solve' contradice la logica terapeutica (no es problema tecnico). 'Attack' es agresivo. 'Erase' implica evitacion. Otras: 'unpack', 'sit with', 'notice'.
examples: Let's explore what that reaction is really about.
Can we unpack what happened with your dad? → typical therapist prompt

questions.text: Instead of pushing through the exhaustion, I've learned to actually rest — proper rest, without guilt.
questions.explanation: Vocabulario wellness maduro. 'Pushing through' (phrasal — forzar), 'proper rest' (proper = de verdad, uso britanico expandido), 'without guilt' (colocacion clave; el guilt sobre descansar es tema recurrente). Contraste 'push through' vs 'rest' es el arc central.
examples: I stopped pushing through and started listening to my body.
Rest without guilt is a skill I'm still learning. → self-awareness

questions.prompt: Wellness coach dice: 'You need to check in with yourself daily.'
questions.question: 'Check in with yourself' means:
options: Pause to notice how you're feeling.
questions.explanation: 'Check in with yourself' = pausar y notar tu estado emocional/fisico. Practica de self-awareness. Tambien 'check in with someone' = preguntar como esta esa persona. Colocacion moderna omnipresente en wellness y liderazgo.
examples: I check in with myself every morning before opening email.
Just checking in — how are you holding up? → mensaje empatico

questions.statement: 'To recharge' can be used metaphorically for humans, meaning to rest and restore energy.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Recharge' aplicado a personas = descansar/reponerse. Metafora de bateria omnipresente. Colocaciones: 'recharge my batteries', 'need to recharge', 'recharge over the weekend'. Es lenguaje neutro-positivo (mas socialmente aceptable que 'necesito parar').
examples: I need the weekend to fully recharge before next week's launch.
A long walk is how I recharge — no phone, just movement. → habit personal

questions.target: Look, I've realized my worth isn't measured by output — resting is productive too, and I'm done apologizing for taking care of myself.
questions.explanation: Discurso wellness assertivo muy actual (nivel podcast/therapy). Estructura: reconocimiento + reframe ('resting is productive') + assertion final. 'I'm done apologizing' es formula empoderada. Colocaciones: 'my worth isn't measured by', 'taking care of myself'.
examples: My worth isn't tied to my calendar — I'm allowed to rest.
I'm done apologizing for boundaries that keep me healthy. → assertion
